steps.text:
Founded the capital and got the empire actually running — it had been idling at zero output.

**Summary:** Founded Nidaros at (65,11) (the advisor's #1 site, score 144 — hills/river, Amber + Salt luxuries, Wheat/Sheep/Stone), set it building a Scout, started Animal Husbandry, and garrisoned the Warrior against a nearby barbarian scout.

Two things worth flagging beyond the summary, since they explain why this turn mattered more than a normal turn 9:

- **The empire was producing nothing.** Turn 9 with zero cities and *no research selected* — science, culture, and gold were all flat zero. That's now +5 gold, 2.5 science, 1.3 culture per turn. The settler had apparently been wandering for 8 turns.
- **The coastal tradeoff was real but not worth taking.** Norway's kit (Longships, Harbor, Stave Church) wants water, and (65,11) is not coastal, so we missed the free Sailing boost. But the advisor ranked the coastal alternative below the current tile, founding there would have cost another turn with a barbarian scout 3 tiles from an undefended settler, and coastal cities can come later. Tempo won.

I did not end the turn, as instructed. Next turn the Warrior auto-continues to the hills at (66,11) as a sentry, and the city needs to reach pop 2 before a Settler becomes available — expansion should be the priority right after the Scout.

steps.text:
I've got a clear picture. Here's what I found and did:

**Situation:** Norway (Harald Hardrada) on Prince, turn 10. One city, one Warrior, 2% of the map explored. Two things stand out as problems:

1. **The capital isn't coastal.** Nidaros at (65,11) is on plains-hills river — good tile, but every neighbor is land. Norway's entire kit is naval (Viking Longships, Knarr ocean travel, Harbor synergy), so none of it is reachable from this city. There's water to the northwest around (64,9)/(65,8) with Amber at (64,8); that's where city #2 should go, but (65,9) is only 2 tiles out and would violate the 3-tile minimum spacing. The scout needs to confirm (65,8) or better before committing.

2. **Dark Age risk.** Era score is 0 against a threshold of 11. Early era score comes almost entirely from exploration — meeting civs, natural wonders, tribal villages, clearing camps — which is another vote for the scout.

**Actions taken:**

- **Warrior** moved from (65,11) to the sheep hills at (66,11), which put it adjacent to the barbarian scout at (67,12). The hills cost both movement points, so it couldn't attack this turn; I fortified it for +4 defense since the moves were spent anyway. It can attack next turn if the barb holds, and it screens the eastern approach either way. The reported barbarian at (66,13) doesn't appear on a fresh map read — it was the same scout's earlier position.
- **Production: left on Scout (4 turns).** Worth flagging why I didn't build a settler: Nidaros is pop 1, and a Settler costs 1 population, so it isn't buildable until pop 2 (~7 turns out). It's genuinely absent from the production list. Separately, `get_global_settle_advisor` returned *no valid settle locations on the revealed map* — we can't plan expansion at all until we see more, so the scout is the actual bottleneck, not growth.
- **Research: left on Animal Husbandry** (9 turns, already 10% in). It unlocks the Pasture for the Sheep the capital is working and reveals Horses for settle planning. At 2.5 science nothing lands quickly, and no alternative pays off sooner.

I considered switching the city to FOOD focus to rush pop 2 and unlock the settler ~2 turns earlier, but it would delay the scout by about the same margin — and since we can't identify a settle site yet, the scout is worth more. Left on default.

**Summary:** Fortified the Warrior on hills at (66,11) adjacent to a barb scout, kept Scout production and Animal Husbandry research (both already optimal — a Settler is impossible at pop 1 and no settle sites are revealed yet), and flagged that the capital is landlocked, which strands Norway's naval kit until a coastal second city goes up near (65,8).

It's genuinely absent from the production list. Separately, `get_global_settle_advisor` returned *no valid settle locations on the revealed map* — we can't plan expansion at all until we see more, so the scout is the actual bottleneck, not growth.
- **Research: left on Animal Husbandry** (9 turns, already 10% in). It unlocks the Pasture for the Sheep the capital is working and reveals Horses for settle planning. At 2.5 science nothing lands quickly, and no alternative pays off sooner.

I considered switching the city to FOOD focus to rush pop 2 and unlock the settler ~2 turns earlier, but it would delay the scout by about the same margin — and since we can't identify a settle site yet, the scout is worth more. Left on default.

Research is Animal Husbandry, already 20% done, which pastures the Sheep the city is working at (66,11).

One thing worth flagging for the turns ahead: **Norway's kit is naval (Viking Longship at Sailing), but Nidaros is not coastal** — that's why the Sailing boost sits at 0%. Sailing costs 20 turns unboosted. The fix is to make the second city coastal (coast sits northwest around (63-65, 9-10)), which halves Sailing and opens the Longship line.

Everything for turn 13 is committed and my warrior is out of moves. Here's what I found and did.

**Situation:** I'm Norway — a naval civ whose whole kit (Longship, Knarr coastal raiding, Harbors, Stave Church) keys off coastal cities — but my capital Nidaros sits inland on river hills at (65,11). That's a structural mismatch worth fixing with city #2.

**What I did:**
- **Warrior** — sent it exploring southwest; it reached the forest-hills at (68,14) and has a standing order toward (66,15). South was walled off by mountains at (68,15)/(69,15), so the river route southwest is the only land path.
- **Capital focus** — set to Food. The city is pop 1, which is exactly why no Settler appeared in the build list (Settlers cost a pop, so they need pop 2). Growth lands in ~4 turns and unlocks expansion.
- **Production and research** — I deliberately left both alone. The Scout completes next turn (switching would waste it), and Animal Husbandry is already 40% done and unlocks the Pasture for the Sheep at (66,11). Code of Laws is the only civic available.

**Two things worth flagging for the turns ahead.** A barbarian Scout is at (67,16), and my capital has no garrison at all — barb scouts report your cities back to camp and trigger raids, so that warrior's hunt is now doubling as defense. I'd build a Slinger once the Scout pops. Separately, era score is 0 against a Dark Age threshold of 11; clearing that barb's camp would help on both fronts.

**Plan for the settler:** the advisor's top coastal site is (69,12) — Amber, Stone, and Sheep in range — and founding there also triggers the Sailing boost, halving the path to Longships.

One-line summary: Scouted southwest with the warrior (spotting a barbarian Scout near my undefended capital), set Nidaros to Food focus to reach pop 2 for a Settler, and kept the 1-turn Scout and Animal Husbandry research — targeting coastal (69,12) as city #2 to unlock Norway's naval kit.

steps.text:
Done. Here's what I found and did.

The big issue was that **Nidaros had an empty production queue** — at 6 production/turn on turn 14, that's pure waste. I started a Builder, since the city has two unimproved resources right next to it (Wheat at (64,11), Sheep at (66,11)), and improving three tiles also boosts the Craftsmanship civic. A Settler isn't selectable yet because the city is pop 1 and a Settler would cost the city its only citizen; it grows to pop 2 in three turns, which is when Settler becomes the right switch.

The Scout was sitting idle inside the city while only 4% of the map was explored, so I set it to automate. That left the capital undefended, so I pulled the Warrior back from (68,14); it ran out of movement at (67,12) and will keep going next turn. That tile also sits between the capital and the best expansion area.

I left research on Animal Husbandry — it's already 50% boosted with 5 turns left, and it unlocks the Pasture for that Sheep tile plus reveals Horses. Switching would throw away the boost.

One thing worth flagging for the next settler decision: **Nidaros is not coastal** (it's on Plains Hills river at (65,11)), which is awkward for Norway, whose whole kit — Longships, Harbors, coastal raiding — needs water. The settle advisor's top site is (68,13) at score 126, but I'd favor **(69,12)** at score 114: it's coastal, still grabs Sheep/Stone/Amber, and it would unlock the Sailing boost ("found a city on the Coast") that we currently can't get. Slightly lower raw yields, much better fit for the civ.

Turn 14: fixed Nidaros's empty build queue (Builder), automated the idle Scout, marched the Warrior back to defend the capital, kept the boosted Animal Husbandry research, and picked coastal (69,12) as the settler target to unlock Norway's naval kit.

steps.text:
Everything's set and I have not ended the turn — that's the host's call.

**What I did and why:**

- **Scout (63,8)** — set to automate. At 5% map explored, continuous exploration is the highest-value thing it can do.
- **Warrior (69,12 → 69,13)** — moved onto coastal hills. That tile is the standout second-city site: it's coastal (Norway's whole kit — Longships, Harbors, and the free Sailing boost — needs coastal cities), sits on hills for defense, and has amber at (70,12), a reef at (71,12), citrus at (70,10), and stone at (68,11) in its work radius, plus a 4-production forest-hill at (68,14). It's 4 tiles from Nidaros, which is clean spacing. The Warrior now holds the spot against barbarians until a settler arrives.
- **Production** — left on Builder. I tried to switch to a Settler and the game refused: a size-1 city can't complete one. Nidaros is at 14/15 food and grows next turn, so the Settler unblocks immediately. The Builder isn't a wasted stopgap either — it improves the unworked wheat at (64,11) and sheep at (66,11), and three improved tiles boosts Craftsmanship.
- **Research** — kept Animal Husbandry. It's 70% done (3 turns) and unlocks the Pasture the Builder needs for that sheep, so switching now would throw away progress and break the sequencing.

**Two things worth flagging for whoever plays turn 17:**

One city at turn 16 is behind, and a Settler for (69,13) should be the very next production choice once the city hits population 2 — that's the single biggest lever available. Separately, era score is 0 against a Dark Age threshold of 11, so some era score needs to come from somewhere in the next stretch. Both policy slots are empty but nothing can fill them yet; they open up when Code of Laws finishes.

steps.text:
Done. Everything's committed for turn 17 without ending it.

What I did and why:

- **Scout** was stranded in dead snow at (64,5) with nothing around it. I walked it two tiles north onto the goody hut at (64,3) and set it to auto-explore. Only 7% of the land is explored and I haven't met a single civ yet — that's also the boost for Writing.
- **Warrior** was already standing in the best land on the map. The settle advisor ranks the southeast cluster #1 through #6, so I moved it one tile to (69,12) — site #2, score 149 — and fortified it to hold the spot against barbarians until a settler arrives. I picked the coastal site over the slightly higher-scoring inland (68,13) on purpose: founding on the coast boosts Sailing, which is the gateway to Longships and Harbors, and Harald's entire kit runs through Harbors.
- **Production**: left the Builder in place (4 turns to go, already about half-paid). Nidaros is flagged for slow growth at 23 turns to the next pop, and it has unimproved Wheat, Sheep, and Salt sitting in its ring. The Builder fixes the growth problem at its root and picks up the Craftsmanship boost for improving 3 tiles. A Settler right now would take 10 turns and drop a pop-2 city to pop 1 with no food engine to recover — Builder first, then Settler toward (69,12).
- **Research**: left Animal Husbandry alone, it's at 80% and lands in 2 turns.

One thing worth flagging for later: era score is 3 with a Dark Age threshold at 11, so I'm 8 short with the Ancient era running out — the goody hut and meeting a civ or two should help.

**One-line summary:** Grabbed a goody hut and automated the Scout, fortified the Warrior on the coastal settle site at (69,12) to reserve it for Norway's Harbor/Longship game, and kept the Builder in Nidaros to fix its 23-turn growth stall before committing to a Settler.

steps.text:
Everything's committed. A note on the two things I deliberately left alone rather than changed:

**Production** — Nidaros is already building a Builder with 3 turns left (~26 of 50 production sunk). Switching to a Settler now would land it around turn 28 versus turn 31 if I let the Builder finish first. I kept the Builder because it fixes the flagged 22-turn growth stall by farming the Wheat at (64,11) and pasturing the Sheep at (66,11), which speeds the Settler back up and also earns the Craftsmanship boost (improve 3 tiles). The Settler goes in next.

**Research** — Animal Husbandry is at 92% and completes next turn. Retargeting now would throw that away, so I left it; it'll want a new pick on turn 19.

Two things worth flagging for whoever picks up turn 19:

- **The brief mentioned a settler — there isn't one.** I have exactly two units, a Scout and a Warrior. One city at turn 18 is genuinely behind, and that's the main strategic problem here.
- **Dark Age risk is live.** Era score is 4 against a Dark Age threshold of 11, so 7 short with the Ancient era running out.

What I did:

- **Promoted the Scout to Ranger** (faster through woods) and set it to automate. At 7% of the map explored, information is the bottleneck.
- **Moved the Warrior from (69,12) to (69,14)** to reveal the southern coastline.

The find worth acting on: the Warrior was standing on settle site #2, **(69,12)** — coastal, score 149, with Amber, Citrus, Fish and a Reef in range. My capital at (65,11) is landlocked, which is a real problem for Norway specifically: it blocks the Sailing boost ("found a city on the Coast"), Harbors, and the Longship kit entirely. Site #1 at (68,13) scores higher (161) but has no water access, so I'd take the coastal site and its civ-kit unlock over the raw score. The active volcano at (68,10) sits two tiles off (69,12) — fertile but a real eruption risk.

One-line summary: Turn 18 as Norway — promoted the Scout to Ranger and automated it, scouted the south coast with the Warrior, and identified coastal (69,12) as the second-city target; left the near-done Builder and 92%-complete Animal Husbandry in place rather than waste their progress.

steps.text:
Done. Here's what I found and did.

**The situation:** Norway (Harald Hardrada) on Prince, turn 19, and the position is behind — one city (Nidaros, pop 2), two units, score 12. Two things were actively broken: **no research was set at all**, so science was being thrown away each turn, and Nidaros is flagged SLOW GROWTH at 21 turns to next pop with three unimproved resources sitting in its borders (Wheat, Sheep, Salt). Era score is 4 against a Dark Age threshold of 11, so that needs attention over the next several turns.

**Actions taken:**
- **Research → Mining** (8 turns). It's cheap, it unlocks the Quarry/Mine that the city needs for its Salt tile, and it opens the whole Masonry / Bronze Working / Wheel tier. Astrology was 38% boosted but 10 turns and less immediately useful.
- **Scout automated** from (64,3). Only 7% of the land is explored, so the information flow matters more than any manual route I'd pick.
- **Warrior moved** from (69,14) to (68,13) — it now sits on the exact tile the settle advisor ranks #1 (score 164), covering the future settle site and closer to home.

**Production left alone deliberately:** Nidaros is 2 turns from finishing a Builder. Switching to a Settler now would delay the improvements that fix the growth problem, and a bigger city makes the settler cheaper to absorb anyway. Builder first, then Settler is the right order.

**For whoever plays turn 20+:** the second city should go at **(69,12)**, not the advisor's #1 pick of (68,13). The advisor scores (68,13) higher (164 vs 152), but it has no water access. (69,12) is coastal, and for Norway that's worth more than the 12-point gap — it boosts Sailing, and Norway gets Harbors at half cost plus Longships. Both sites reach the same Citrus, Sheep, Stone, Horses, Amber and Fish.

One-line summary: Set research to Mining (was unset and wasting science), automated the scout, and advanced the warrior to the top-ranked settle area at (68,13) — leaving the near-complete Builder in production, with (69,12) as the recommended coastal second-city site for Norway.

steps.text:
Done. Here's what I found and did.

The situation is behind schedule: turn 20 with a single city and no settler. Nidaros sits on river hills at (65,11) but is **landlocked** — awkward for Norway, whose whole kit (Longships, Harbors, coastal raiding) needs water. Meanwhile the entire east coast is unclaimed and rich: Amber, Fish, Horses, Stone, and Citrus all cluster around (69,12).

**Actions taken:**
- **Scout** at (64,3) was stranded in a snow dead-end with nothing left to find, so I set it to automate. It had already revealed Eyjafjallajökull, which is why Astrology sits pre-boosted at 38%.
- **Warrior** moved from (68,13) to (69,12) and fortified — it now holds the future city site, reveals the surrounding coast, and is in position to escort the settler when it arrives.

**Deliberately left alone**, since both were already correct:
- **Production** stays on Builder — it completes this turn, so overriding it would throw away 50 production. It has three unimproved resources waiting (Wheat, Sheep, Salt), which fixes the slow-growth warning and earns the Craftsmanship boost. Settler should follow immediately next turn.
- **Research** stays on Mining (7 turns, already 16% in). It unlocks the Salt luxury for amenities plus mines on the many hills, and it opens Masonry/Bronze Working/Wheel. Sailing is the natural follow-up — founding that coastal city boosts it from 17 turns down to roughly half.

One caution worth flagging: era score is 4 against a Dark Age threshold of 11, so seven more points are needed before the era flips.

**Summary:** Automated the snowbound scout, fortified the warrior on the coastal settle site at (69,12) to hold it for the settler, and kept Builder/Mining as-is since both were already the optimal call.
